checks.reason: seedOffset is literally a_j + m b_j - 2 a_j j; seed_step_offset gives gamma^(N+delta_j). Native bounds are -3m² <= delta_j <= m². The exact quotient-row relation gives N = m²c_j - jm b_j + j²a_j. Exact offset periodicity and representative periodicity make the polynomial coefficients depend only on m,n,j. A unit n makes a_j a nonzero canonical residue.

publicRowModulus is the least prime above the ceiling sixth-root, so its exact bin is (mminus)^6 < pq <= m^6. Since p >= cX, its q strip has length <= 6m^5g/(cX); dividing by m² gives <= A0 g and hence at most A1(g+1) integer representatives of each q class. Consecutive selector-prime gaps telescope; adding their count gives sum(g+1) <= 2b0 M. No short-interval prime equidistribution is used.
p>m implies m does not divide p. If m divides p-1 = v R_p, primality of m and R_p, R_p>m and v<m are contradictory. Thus p mod m is neither 0 nor 1, excluding j=1 repeated-root degeneracy.

The actual local period is exactly R_p and p=1 mod R_p, so gamma^(N+delta_j)=alpha^r iff q+delta_j-m²r = K R_p. Dependence of gamma on q does not affect this equivalence. With r<L<=4m², |q+delta_j-m²r| <= X+3m²+4m^4. R_p >= cX/(2v) and m³<=b0³X yield |K| <= C2 v m. Integer K count is <= CK vm.

Multiplying q+delta_j-m²r = K R_p by vp gives vpq+vp delta_j = Kp(p-1) mod m². Since pq=n mod m² this is exactly F(p)=Kp²-(K+v delta_j)p-vn=0 mod m². The constant term is a unit modulo m because v<m and n is a unit. Removing r introduces no omitted coverage condition; all true hits obey the same necessary polynomial and global K bound.

For fixed m,n,j,v,K, the nonzero polynomial modulo prime m has at most two simple roots. Taylor expansion F(x+mt)=F(x)+mt Fprime(x) mod m² gives exactly one lift per simple root. CRT with p=1 mod v has spacing vm². Since X<=a0^-3 m³ and v<m, each class has <= C3 m/v integer p representatives.

Summing <=2 C3 m/v representatives over <= CK vm multipliers gives <=2 C3 CK m² p/K incidences per m,n,j,v. Multiplying by <=m² states, <=H_X rows in each state, <=V cofactors and A1(g+1) q representatives, then telescoping gaps, gives exactly the stated bound 4 A1 C3 CK b0^5 H_X V M^5. All r<L are included without an additional L factor. Catalog variation with BOTH digits is fully paid by the m² state sum.

At a repeated root x, F(x)=Fprime(x)=0 implies Kx²=-vn and K(2x-1)=v delta_j. Thus x and K are units. Substitute n=a_j j² and delta_j=a_j(1-2j) modulo m to obtain (2j-1)x²-2j²x+j²=(x-j)((2j-1)x-j)=0. These two branches exhaust repeated roots; K=0 cannot be repeated because the constant coefficient is a unit.

At x=j modulo m, repeatedness implies F(p)=F(j) modulo m². Substitution of the literal row relation gives F(j)=(K+v a_j)j(j-1) modulo m². j and j-1 are units, so m² divides K+v a_j. Since |K+v a_j| <= (C2+1)vm < m² eventually, K=-v a_j as an integer. Substituting into the exact hit recovers m²r=a_j p+mb_j-2a_j j+q.

For fixed m,n and a selected j, p=j modulo m has <=X/m+1<=C3 m² integer representatives. Every actual p is counted once after dropping period and primality restrictions; no v summation remains. States, selected rows, selector q class occupancy and gap telescoping give 2 A1 C3 b0^5 H_X M^5 for one orientation.

The second branch has d=2j-1 a unit and x0=j/d modulo m². Repeatedness gives F(x0)=F(p)=0 modulo m². Clearing d² gives -j(j-1)[K+v a_j d²-2vmb_jd], exactly matching the authoritative native second_branch_cleared_multiplier_identity. Because x is neither 0 nor 1, j,j-1,d are units.

At fixed a_j,j the lower state s=a_j j² mod m is fixed. Subtracting the exact row relations for n=s+mu and n0=s+mu0 gives u-u0=-j(b_j(n)-b_j(n0)) modulo m. Hence b_j modulo m permutes all m residues. Since m is odd and v,d nonzero, K=-v a_j d²+2vmb_jd modulo m² runs through all m lifts of the fixed nonzero K class modulo m.

The K interval |K|<=C2vm contains at most CK v representatives of its fixed mod-m class. Each fixes at most one upper digit. Thus fixed m,v has <=CK v m² (n,j,K) incidences over all original rows. p lies in one mod-m class and 1 mod-v class, so spacing vm gives <=C3 m²/v representatives. The v factors cancel; summing <=V cofactors and selector gaps gives 2 A1 C3 CK b0^5 V M^5. Neither a catalog row factor nor a column factor is needed.

Adding the simple and both repeated branches, and both hidden-field orientations, gives 4 A1 C3 b0^5 [2CK H_X V + H_X + CK V] M^5 = O((H_X+1)V M^5). Since V=O(M^(3-3kappa)), division by Omega(M^6/log²M) gives O((H_X+1) M^(2-3kappa) log²M). Under eta<3kappa-2=.031 this tends to zero for every fixed logarithmic power. Positive actual mass remains at unbounded scales; all selected row-column differences are nonzero in both fields.

Read the preserved primary PDF and fresh pdftotext output: Kurlberg-Pomerance Section 4 Lemma 19 explicitly records positive-proportion primes with a prime divisor of p-1 above p^.677, and Lemma 20 discards base-e order omissions at O(x^.646/log x). Choosing c small and a finite ratio<=3/2 partition gives balanced prime-pair mass Omega(X²/log²X) along unbounded scales. This uses classical published density, not a Lean axiom or a claim of Lean-proved infinitude.

The large prime R_P is unique and occurs to exponent one because kappa>1/2. Base-2 order omissions have order <=V; the logarithm of product_(r<=V)(2^r-1) gives O(V²/log X) prime loss. Diagonal and cross-period pairs cost O(X^(2-kappa)+X). Since v_P<m, the actual factorial projection kills every small cofactor part and preserves R_P. Cross exclusions ensure R_P does not divide N-1. The actual projected local orders are precisely distinct R_p,R_q>16m², so the previously audited short/projection route returns actual longBase 2.

Balanced ratio<=3/2 and pq<=m^6 imply p,q <= sqrt(3/2)m³ <1.5m³, while p,q~M³ give m²<=p,q eventually. The native balanced_forced_seed_prime_hit gives one original hit below L at each factor tag. Thus full A_all is zero in both fields. Every selected A_S is a unit by all-hit absence, so A_all=A_S A_complement forces A_complement=0 modulo N. Selected scalar gcds are 1 and complements are N. Multiplication and division by certified units preserve the unit-or-zero class; arbitrary additive observations remain outside the conclusion.

For s=N mod m nonzero, sigma_s(j)=s/j is an involution on nonzero tags and maps the actual p tag to the q tag. Any orbit cover with fixed points included retains at least one factor tag. On the balanced gates either retained factor tag has its forced index below L, so the partial norm is nonunit. The number of fixed points of j²=s is 0 or 2 for odd prime m; every orbit cover has minimum (m-1+f_s)/2, attained by canonical smaller endpoints. When s is a nonresidue, Legendre signs reverse and the quadratic-residue set is a minimum cover. Computing the public mask requires Otilde(m) bit work, without claiming the partial norm can be acquired at that cost.

The authoritative isolated-row family has a common G of m-o(m) original rows, with all J=Theta(m) points of each G row globally unique in both fields at width4m. Every orbit-cover mask has Theta(m) retained isolated rows, regardless of full-N endpoint choice. Nonzero local weights at those retained labels force at least |S intersect G|J poles and hence normalized exact whole-series denominator degree Omega(m²). Summing separate denominator degrees over a mask family whose union is an orbit cover also yields Omega(m²). This is a dense exact-carrier write/storage obstruction, not an implicit partial-norm or factoring lower bound.

The theorem is for each fixed accessible row union S_(m,n), not a universal single input avoiding every possible catalog. Full-N adaptation is covered only inside that fixed union. A full-N recipe with executed singleton support but per-state accessible union of all m rows is outside the theorem. The orbit-cover gate is sufficient rather than necessary. On unbalanced inputs only the smaller factor has the known short forced index; selecting the larger tag alone is not certified. The document expressly preserves these limits.

checks.reason: For odd finite order R, product_(s<R)(a^s T-a^r)=T^R-1: its leading factor a^(R(R-1)/2)=1, and reciprocal shifted powers enumerate all R distinct roots. Interchanging r,s gives the exact identity Norm_R(P_L)=(T^R-1)^L for all L.

At x^R=1 and characteristic not dividing R, (x+z)^R-1 has linear coefficient R/x nonzero. Raising to L gives zero Hasse jets below L and coefficient (R/x)^L at L. The ordinary Lth derivative requires L! nonzero, as explicitly assumed. The low head is independent of original interval membership.

For coprime odd local orders A,B, H=AB. The global cycle reduces to B repetitions of the A cycle at p and A repetitions of the B cycle at q. Thus C_H mod p=(T^A-1)^B and Norm_H(P_L) mod p=(T^A-1)^(LB), with the symmetric q formulas. These exact identities account for repeated roots and leading units.

Assume p<q. Since A divides p-1 and B divides q-1, q does not divide H. At any local point x^B=1, C_H has multiplicity A>1 and zero derivative, but (T^H-1)prime(x)=H/x is nonzero. The proposed binomial equality is therefore false even with exact global-order advice.

Native CoreData/LongData gives coprime rough local periods >4m² with no prime factors <=m, hence odd; the m² power preserves both orders and generates the same local subgroup as gamma. Every original target is in that subgroup. The target-carrier completion for d retained tags is (T^A-1)^(dB) and (T^B-1)^(dA), including duplicate tags. Its jets below d min(A,B) vanish modulo N. Even d=1 has every Otilde(m)-length global jet head saturated. Original finite-interval partial norms are expressly not this completion.

On the distinct prime-period family, gcd(N,alpha^R_p-1)=p, since R_q does not divide R_p. Native global_order_totient_and_sum and sumSignal_eq_sum show a supplied exact global order H yields (N+1) mod H=p+q. This is existing factor recovery, and no cost-free period acquisition is claimed.

For fixed m,n, at most T_X/log R0 distinct primes >=R0 divide any nonzero exponent in the catalog, by the logarithm of their product. Each such R permits <=X/R<=V prime candidates p=1 mod R. With p>m, fixed n fixes one q class modulo m², containing <=X/m²+1=O(M) integers. Counting O(M) selectors and O(M²) states yields O(V T_X M^4/log M) bad pairs in one orientation, with a factor two for both.

If T_X=O(M^tau log^a M), the bad exponent is 7-3kappa+tau, smaller than 6 exactly when tau<3kappa-1=1.031. Soft-linear exponent-bit budget tau=1 therefore gives exponent5.969. Removing these pairs leaves actual inputs on which every catalogued exponent is coprime to both prime periods and alpha^E-1 is a unit. Negative exponents use absolute values; zero is explicitly excluded; full-N exponent recipes and ring-additive observations are outside scope.

Starting from one generator and identity, g multiplication/inversion gates bound every output exponent magnitude by 2^g; each multiplication can at most double the prior maximum and inversion preserves magnitude. A polylogarithmic output count with Otilde(m) gates has soft-linear total exponent-bit budget. Other group inputs, coefficient-ring additions and arbitrarily many outputs are explicitly outside this consequence.

hit_multiplier_polynomial_identity is the exact ring identity obtained from p-1=vR and q+delta-m²r=KR. The retained residue is -v p m²r, so reducing modulo m² eliminates r without omitting any original column. The modEq theorem uses p q congruent n and the correct Int.ModEq divisibility convention n-pq.

For two roots in one mod-m class, their polynomial-value difference factors (p-p0)c with c=K(p+p0)-(K+v delta). c is congruent to Fprime(p0) mod m and therefore nonzero under the explicit simple-root premise. Existing integer_coprime_square cancels c modulo m². The resulting unique-lift statement is arithmetic only, with no unproved existence, primality density or Hensel algorithm cost.

multiplier_repeated_root_branches eliminates K using the exact polynomial and derivative equalities, obtaining v a (x-j)((2j-1)x-j)=0. v and a nonzero are explicit. The field product-zero law gives x=j or (2j-1)x=j. This remains valid in characteristic two; only later second-branch carry counting needs odd m.

omitted_root_unit and added_root_unit use the divisibility of g-u or g+u into g^(2m)-u^(2m)=a^m-1. An explicit unit a^m-1 therefore makes both linear punctures units in any commutative ring, including rings with zero divisors. complete_square_unit and omitted_root_map_unit respectively certify the complete unit and its image under a multiplicative homomorphism.

In a finite field, a nonzero mth root has order dividing prime m and the group cardinality. If m does not divide the latter, the root must be one. This matches finite_group_no_prime_root and finite_field_no_prime_root. root_free_scalar_gate_unit then makes a^m-1 a unit whenever a!=1, with the base no-root premise explicit.

With m and R prime, 0<v<m<R, m cannot divide vR: it divides neither positive v<m nor the distinct larger prime R. For P-1=vR, the hidden base field has no nontrivial mth roots. The exclusion is pointwise and requires no B_m exceptional-set estimate.

Under m+1

=2, epsilon*m is not one for either epsilon=+1 or -1. Odd m gives (epsilon*m)^m=epsilon*m^m. Hence signed_gauss_scalar_gate_unit proves the exact public integer gate epsilon*m^m-1 is a unit at each hidden prime. No effective phase or primitive-root embedding is needed for this scalar gate.

On the inherited published source, v_P,v_Q=O(M^.969), R_P,R_Q=Omega(M^2.031), P,Q~M³. For every fixed comparable range aM<=m<=bM with a>0, all sufficiently large scales simultaneously satisfy v_P,v_Q<m<R_P,R_Q and m+1<P,Q. Therefore every auxiliary prime in this range satisfies the pointwise gate, including full-N adaptive choices; no small fixed auxiliary catalog is needed.

For the honest Gauss element, the classical square identity is G(s)^2=epsilon*m at nonzero phase. Any mth root u satisfies u^m=1, so the unit scalar gate forbids both G(s)-u and G(s)+u. Complete G(s) is a unit from its unit square. This permits adaptive phase/root/sign choices but excludes arbitrary multi-puncture combinations or additive observations. Native gate lemmas retain the Gauss square as an explicit premise.

The finite formulas Q_s=zeta^-s G(s)-1, trace(Q_s)=1 and trace(G(s))=0 at nonzero phase follow from complete root sums. At phase zero, Q_0=m-1 and G_0=m, with traces (m-1)² and m(m-1); all are units under P,Q>m. Determinant norms map units to units, whereas traces are handled by their explicit formulas, not by a false multiplicative-homomorphism argument.

GaussCompositeBridge.part proves the scalar gate is a unit modulo p*q from its nonzero prime reductions, then maps that gate to any commutative coefficient-ring extension. semiprime_gauss_puncture_unit concludes both punctures are units with g²=f(epsilon*m) and u^m=1 explicit. It does not instantiate a concrete cyclotomic Gauss element, norm implementation, trace formulas or actual prime-family infinitude.

checks.reason: At nonzero phase, only t=0 has zero exponent. Trace of each nonzero-phase root is -1 and trace(1)=m-1. Summing over distinct tags, including phase duplicates, gives removed trace m*k0-k and remaining trace k-m*k0. For 1<=k<m both possible integers are nonzero with absolute value below each hidden prime. This is a simultaneous identity for every puncture, including adaptive choices.

For termwise moment indices with r divisible by m, the remaining element is m-k and its trace is (m-k)(m-1). For k<m, each factor is positive and below each hidden prime, so the product is a unit without requiring the product itself to be smaller than the primes. k=m gives zero. Empty and full punctures never give a proper trace gcd.

If g²=a, u^m=1 and g=±c*u with nonzero base c, then (a/c²)^m=1. The root-free base field forces a=c². For c=2, a=epsilon*m cannot equal 4 when P>m+4 and m is odd prime. Thus G_s-2u is nonzero in every hidden extension. Equal-phase distinct quadratic tags t and -t are covered.

If g=1+u and g²=a scalar, u=1 would force a=4, excluded. Otherwise u has order m. Frobenius gives g^P=±g. The positive case forces m|(P-1), contradicting the root-free premise. The negative case yields u^P=-u-2 and u^(P²)=u, so m|(P²-1). With prime m and m not dividing P-1, P=-1 mod m, hence u^P=u^-1. Therefore (u+1)²=0, forcing g²=0, contradicting a=±m nonzero.

The double-puncture proofs apply to every primitive-root realization, since they use only the Gauss square and mth-root identities. At each hidden characteristic P!=m, the cyclotomic algebra is a product of finite extension fields because Phi_m is separable. Nonvanishing in every component makes the puncture a unit. Applying this at both hidden primes makes its determinant norm a unit modulo the actual distinct-prime N.

The inherited actual family has P-1=vR with 0<v<m<R and R,m prime, so m does not divide P-1; likewise for Q. Its sufficiently large inputs satisfy P,Q>m+4. The claims are classical and concern unweighted trace punctures and the specified two double-puncture norm classes. They neither close distinct nonzero-phase double-puncture norms nor transfer to original full-carry source moments.
